lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 87, which keeps a pull request session's context small, so it costs less.
It has three parts: what the PR adds, how it was checked, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
A new Context section in CLAUDE.md, a new build-verify agent, and quieter log reading in two skills.
First, a noisy command writes everything to a log file and echoes only its exit code.
The session reads that exit code first, to see whether the command passed.
Then it reads the last 30 lines, or on a failure, the lines its skill's grep picks out.
lines.say: Then it reads the last thirty lines, or on a failure, the lines its skill's grep picks out.

lines.caption: So the context holds the exit code and a few lines, never the whole log.
Second, heavy steps move into subagents, starting with the new build-verify agent, which builds and runs the tests.
The local review of the diff runs in a fresh agent that returns only its findings.
The explainer page and its narration are written by a subagent too.
Each sends back a short answer, with any failing lines copied exactly, not paraphrased.
Third, reads stay narrow: grep for a function, then read only its lines.
And the main session never opens a screenshot; subagents read those instead.
Every turn re-reads the whole context, and one batch session reached about 567k tokens and cost about $33.6.
lines.say: Every turn re-reads the whole context, and one batch session reached about five hundred sixty-seven thousand tokens, and cost about thirty-three dollars sixty.

lines.caption: The batch skill's brief now points every group's session to these rules.
A redirect keeps a command's exit code, while a pipe into tail hides it, so logs go to a file first.
Build, test, render and narration commands all log to a file, and the exit code is always read first.
On a failure, each skill or agent names its own grep, so only the failing lines come back.
build-verify installs and runs the tests only in a cloud container, and never edits, commits or pushes.
The review agent and the explainer subagent work the same way, and this page was written by one.
Their fixed short answers keep confident wording from hiding a real failure.
Reads use grep first, then a slice of the file, and screenshots stay with the subagents.
In the grep table, visual-verify's pattern keeps only the failing tests' lines and the count.
build-verify's test pattern keeps every result line, passes too.
Its build pattern finds real errors, not every compile command that turns warnings into errors.
And the narration check's pattern keeps every stale line and the verdict.
build-verify always answers in this fixed shape, ending with the exact failing lines.
Outside a cloud container it skips install and verify, since install replaces the system's Thunar.
The PR changes CLAUDE.md and three skills and adds the agent, plus this page and its narration.
To undo it, revert the PR, and sessions go back to printing output inline.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It follows the pr-digest agent, the screenshot auditors, and the test script's own result lines.
The building session grepped a 9-line sample test log, and visual-verify's pattern kept 7 lines, dropping both passes.
lines.say: The building session grepped a nine-line sample test log, and visual-verify's pattern kept seven lines, dropping both passes.

lines.caption: build-verify's pattern kept all 9 lines of the same log.
lines.say: build-verify's pattern kept all nine lines of the same log.

lines.caption: A redirect kept the failing exit code of 1, while a pipe into tail showed 0.
lines.say: A redirect kept the failing exit code of one, while a pipe into tail showed zero.

lines.caption: The Thunar build and the new agent itself were not run: no code changed, and agents load at session start.
A fresh review agent found 7 problems, 2 of them high, and all 7 were fixed.
lines.say: A fresh review agent found seven problems, two of them high, and all seven were fixed.

lines.caption: Several greps matched the wrong lines, so now each skill or agent gives its own, and no stale line is dropped.
build-verify could have installed on the owner's machine, and now it installs only in a cloud container.
Smaller gaps were closed, and the explainer's render check now always runs in its subagent.
CI's own findings will be in the code review comment on pull request 87.
The build-verify agent first runs in the next pull request session, after the merge.
The real test is the next batch group's context and cost, against 567k tokens and $33.6 for #82.
lines.say: The real test is the next batch group's context and cost, against five hundred sixty-seven thousand tokens and thirty-three dollars sixty for number 82.

lines.caption: On the pull request, the summary comment says build and verify found no code to build.
Part 3. What comes later.
No issue builds on this one, and the next batch group is the first to measure it.
If sessions still near compaction, splitting each group into an implementing and a review session may follow.
In short: logs stay in files, heavy work goes to subagents, and sessions read only what they need.
